links.outcome: Whether expert review/correction of AI contours catches errors; need for correction of AI segmentation
links.effect: Reference contours made by expert correction of AI-seg; AI-seg HD outliers >30 mm in liver (3/23) and spleen (2/23) due to hepatomegaly; corrected AI workflow reduced total time to 47.0 vs 54.3 min (p=0.014).
links.quote: Cases in which AI segmentation showed outlier liver (3/23) and spleen (2/23) HD (HD > 30.0 mm) were due to hepatomegaly caused by metastatic whole liver tumors.

links.outcome: AI segmentation compared with manual contouring by physicists/technologists on accuracy, dose and time
links.effect: AI-seg median DSC liver 0.988, spleen 0.965, kidneys 0.994 vs manual 0.955, 0.929, 0.929; AI with correction faster (47.0 vs 54.3 min, p=0.014).
links.quote: Further, the total required time for the reference contour, including the corrections after AI segmentation, was significantly shorter than that for manual contouring ( p = 0.014).

links.outcome: AI segmentation failures in hepatomegaly requiring human correction
links.effect: AI-seg HD exceeded 30 mm in liver (3/23) and spleen (2/23); spleen Dmax significantly lower in AI-seg (p<0.001), so AI contours need physician review.
links.quote: However, the inadequate contouring of the whole liver and spleen is clinically unacceptable.
